description.narrative: The Project Development Objectives are: (a) to strengthen the property rights of the population in the Project area through improved regularization, titling, and registry services; and (b) to improve Nicaragua's capacity to respond promptly and effectively to an eligible emergency.

The objectives of the Second Land Administration Project for Nicaragua are: (a) to strengthen the property rights of the population in the project area through improved regularization, titling, and registry services; and (b) to improve Nicaragua's capacity to respond promptly and effectively to an eligible emergency. There are five components to the project, the first component being consolidation of the institutional and policy framework. The second component is the strengthening of property registration and alternative conflict resolution capacity. The third component is the titling and regularization services. The fourth component is the project management, monitoring and evaluation. Finally, the fifth component is the contingency emergency response component. This component will finance public and private sector expenditures on a positive list of goods, both domestic and imported, and/or specific works, goods, services (including audit costs) and emergency operation costs required for Nicaragua's emergency recovery. A Contingency Emergency Response Component (CERC) operational manual will apply to this component, detailing financial management, procurement, safeguard and any other necessary implementation arrangements.

title.narrative: Time to disburse funds requested by Government for an eligible emergency

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved (n/a). The Government requested on June 22, 2020, the activation of the Contingency Emergency Response Component (CERC)to fund eligible activities related to the novel Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) response. The approval for this CERC was faster than normal because the Bank recognized eligible expenses already incurred by the government. The  CERC was triggered on June30, 2020, in an amount of US$ 1,450,000.00 of uncommitted funds. This amount was reallocated from Disbursement Category (1) to Category (2), as stated in the withdrawal table included in Section IV A. 2 of Schedule 2 of the Financing Agreement of the additional financing credit.</p>

title.narrative: Households with surveyed parcels report a substantial improvement in land tenure security

comment.narrative: <p>100% Achieved: At the end of the Project, WB, FAO, and the UCP under PGR  designed an impact evaluation to assess the Efficiency of combined investments in the modernization of land administration systems and land tenure rights formalization. This study consisted of a beneficiary survey of 1,014 households (560 rural and 454 urban, 47% women and 53% men) within the departments coveredby Phases 1 and 2 of PRODEP (treatment and control groups), which assessed both the evolution of the land transactions in the property registry (RPP)  of Chinandega and the tax collection by municipalities (including counterfactuals). The study provided valuable information about the short and long-term effects of the land tenure regularization on the main households’ assets, the increase in the formalization of land transactions in the Chinandega SIICAR, and the municipalities' capacity to collect land taxes (see Annexes 4 and 5).</p>

title.narrative: Grievances registered related to delivery of project benefits addressed (%)

comment.narrative:
<p>Fully achieved: 3,750 (out of 3,750) grievances were received, attended and resolved through the GRM (SAPP); of which 1,628 (43%) were presented by women and 2,122 (57%) by men.</p>

<p>The Project had the GRM in place from 2014 to 2020, referred to by the Government as "Sistema de Atención al Protagonista PRODEP (SAPP)". SAPP could be accessed through: (i) three telephonelines (1 toll-free); (ii) offices in the municipalities participating in the project; (iii) regional offices in the departments within the project area; and (iv) field teams during the systematic cadastre and regularization process.</p>

<p>All cases were enteredinto an electronic database that allowed data analysis and reporting. The average number of cases received per day was four. The average resolution time per case was 2 days.</p>

title.narrative: Number of households receiving legal documents through the Project

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The Project issued 120,965 legal land documents (102% achieved), of which 92,022 were new titles (109% achieved), and 47,851 were for women, either individually or as a couple (104% achieved).</p>

title.narrative: The database of fiscal cadastre is increased by participating municipalities

comment.narrative: <p>487% (170.37%/35%) Achieved: 20 Municipalities increased by 170.37% the database of their fiscal municipal cadastre. Target 35%: 123,081 parcels, achieved 170.37%: 209,691 parcels.</p>

title.narrative: Baseline for project impact evaluation, Mid-term Report, and Final Evaluation Report completed in a timely and satisfactory manner

comment.narrative: <p>100% Achieved: The baseline was accomplished by the Project through a series of evaluations, by Indicator, from 2013 to 2015. And, the MTR (January-February, 2016) and the Final Evaluation (January-June, 2020) were completed and performed by firms and external consultants.</p>

title.narrative: Complementary areas in the indigenous territories in the Special Development Zone of Bosawas are demarcated and titled

comment.narrative:
<p>100% Achieved: Two complementary areas of the indigenous territories in the Special Development Zone of Bosawas were demarcated and titled, which strengthened indigenous peoples' land rights.</p>
<p> </p>

title.narrative: Land parcels with use or ownership rights recorded as a result of the project

comment.narrative:
<p>123% Achieved: Records were formalized for 229,699 land parcels with use or ownership rights, of which 95,678 (target 40%, achieved 42%) were for women (128% achieved), through the cadastral surveying and land regularization processes.</p>
<p>In addition, thecadastre was completed in six (6) Indigenous communities of the country’s Pacific-Central region, following a culturally appropriate and acceptable participatory process.</p>

title.narrative: Protected areas are demarcated and registered in the database of the National System of Protected Areas

comment.narrative:
<p>100% Achieved: The demarcation of all the five protected areas in the departments of Nueva Segovia, Jinotega, and Rivas under the Project was completed and registered in the National System of Protected Areas, implementing good environmental practices and following the processes outlined in the Manual for the Demarcation of Protected Areas.</p>

<p>The demarcation of the five Protected Areas was combined with the implementation of a communication strategy to raise awareness about the environment, with a gender participation approach. Other environmental management activities were implemented, such as training, certification of materials for the construction of landmarks and signs, integral management of solid waste, mitigation and prevention measures in waste management issues,implementation of occupational health and safety measures.</p>

<p>Additionally, three collaborative management agreements were signed to strengthen and promote collaboration mechanisms between the Ministry of the Environment and Natural Resources (MARENA), Municipalities, and Community leaders.</p>

title.narrative: Conflict resolution agreements, pre-qualified as registrable, are formalized in the Property Registry

comment.narrative: <p>Fully Achieved: 72% of conflict resolution agreements were pre-qualified and recorded in the Property Registry (target 70%). This indicator was achieved through the carrying out of mediation services during the cadastral and regularization processes underthe Project, including: (i) the provision of conflict resolution training to mediators and Co-executing Agencies’ staff; and (ii) the preparation of a manual to standardize mediation results.</p>

<p>94% achieved., The Project benefited 952,814 people (end target: 1,016,000) of which 478,408 are women (98% achieved). The shortfall (63,186 people) resulted from delays in the cadastral surveying of the rural areas of the Jinotega municipality. The processes of dialogue and consultation with the Indigenous Peoples in Jinotega took longer than expected, and the cadastre could not be completed before the end of the project. However, thanks to the additional financing, the Project benefited an additional 202,814 Nicaraguans, compared to the original credit target of 750,000 people.</p>

title.narrative: SIICAR is redesigned satisfactorily in terms of operations security, business objectives, and policies and procedures

comment.narrative:
<p>95% Achieved: The new Integrated Cadastre and Registry Information System (SIICAR 2.0) was evaluated through an external audit firm; which demonstrated that SIICAR 2.0 was redesigned satisfactorily (95%), in terms of: operations security (91%), business objectives (94%), and policies and procedures (100%), according to ISO/IEC 27002; SIICAR 2.0 was developed and established in two of the most important departments of the country: 51% in Managua (target 50%, achieved=101%), and 15% in Estelí (target 15%, achieved=100%).; and consolidated in Chinandega (target 100%, achieved=100%),</p>

<p>Through the redesigned SIICAR 2.0 the following subsystems were developed:</p>

<p>Registration (property, commercial, private, certificates, registration advertising), Customer service (private component, online services), Administration, Operations, Query, Public services: digitization, NGOs, Physical cadastre, SIICAR GEO (geospatial viewer and map maintenance tool), SIICAR CAT, SIICAR CONS, and Cadastral digitization.</p>

<p>The original Indicator was: SIICAR consolidated in Chinandega and expanded to at least three more departments (Unit of Measure: Number). Original target: 4. Achieved: 1 (25%).</p>

<p>This Indicator was revised in the Second Project Restructuring, approved on November 10, 2016, with a target of 75%; and its end target increased to 100% on June 26, 2017 through the Additional Financing.</p>

title.narrative: Reduction in number of days to issue a cadastral certificate

comment.narrative: <p>86% Achieved: The number of days to issue a cadastral certificate was reduced from 12 to 7 days (baseline 12 days, target 6 days).</p>

title.narrative: Avg no. of days to complete recording of purchase/sale of property in land adm systm

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. Registry processes, counting on an updated and integrated database and the availability of qualified technical personnel, allowed a substantial reduction in time to complete the recording of purchase/sale of properties in the land administration system. Therefore, the number of days to complete the recording of the purchase-sale of properties was reduced from 50 to 18 days (baseline 50 days, revised target 25 days, achieved 18 days = 139%).</p>

title.narrative: SIICAR is evaluated independently as satisfactory in terms of operation, data and security

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. This indicator was evaluated through an independent firm which demonstrated that SIICAR II is satisfactory (93%) in terms of: operation (89%), data (100%) and security (91%), according to ISO / IEC 27002.</p>

title.narrative: CERC established and ready to provide access to financial resources to Nicaragua in case of an eligible emergency

comment.narrative: <p>Fully achieved. A country-level CERC Manual was prepared and kept updated; and training was provided to the Ministry of Finance as the Coordinating Agency for the CERC. Several CERCs have been maintained across the country’s portfolio. This facilitated the rapid activation of the CERC following the Government’s request during the last week of project implementation. Thus, the CERC was activated on June 30, 2020, to support the Government's overall response to the COVID-19 pandemic, in the amount of US$ 1,450,000.00 of uncommitted funds.</p>

title.narrative: Establishment of SISCAT (municipal cadasre)-SISCAF (national cadastre) link

comment.narrative: <p>136% Achieved: The project linked the cadastre of 15 Municipalities to the national cadastre system under INETER. This is a new Indicator, included in the Additional Financing.</p>

title.narrative: Technical acceditations issued by INETER to staff of municipalities

comment.narrative: <p>120% Achieved: 24 Municipalities benefited from accreditation on cadastral technical capacity (Target 20: 120% achieved). This is a new Indicator, included in the Additional Financing.</p>
